mainKeyword: Black and Decker cordless string trimmer
guideTitle: Best Black and Decker Cordless String Trimmers (2026)
metaDescription: Six Black+Decker cordless string trimmers across the 20V MAX and 40V MAX lines, compared on feed system, power dial, reach and battery value for lawns.
expertTake: The 40V MAX 13 inch kit with a charge indicator is the best all-round Black+Decker string trimmer, and the 20V MAX EASYFEED 12 inch is the value pick for small lawns. The telescoping 40V model is the one for tall users. Anyone with brush, blackberry or heavy weeds should skip the brand's line trimmers and look at a brushless or gas machine.
introParagraphs: A string trimmer is one of the simplest powered tools, but small design choices decide whether it is a pleasure or a chore: how the line feeds, how the shaft adjusts, and how much battery you get. One brand can offer very different answers to those questions across its range.
The right choice depends on yard size, the height of the person using it and whether you also want a sweeper or edger. This guide sorts six models from one maker by those practical questions.

products.name: Black+Decker 40V MAX 13 in. String Trimmer and Lawn Edger Kit, Charge Indicator
products.description:
This is the Black+Decker string trimmer that suits the most yards. A 13 inch cutting swath is wide enough to cover a lawn border quickly, and a power drive transmission raises torque at the string so the head holds speed when it meets thick, wet grass. The 40V MAX battery has a state-of-charge indicator, which tells you at a glance whether you can finish the front edge.

The tool converts from trimmer to edger in seconds, which matters more than it sounds: edging a driveway with the head turned and a wheel guide is the job where small string trimmers earn their keep. The kit includes a battery and charger, so there is nothing to add.

The tradeoff is weight and reach against the 20V models: a 40V battery is bigger, and the shaft is fixed length, so a tall user has to bend more than with the telescoping sibling. Replace the line with the maker's spools, clean grass from under the guard after each use and store the battery indoors. For a mid-sized lawn, it is the one to buy first. The charge indicator also helps you plan the order of the job, so you can edge the long driveway first and trim the small beds with whatever remains. Over several seasons it is the pack that ages first, so avoid leaving it on the charger over winter.
products.bestFor: Mid-sized lawns that need trimming and edging from one tool.
pros: Power drive transmission adds torque at the string
State-of-charge indicator on the battery
Converts from trimmer to edger quickly
Battery and charger included
cons: Fixed shaft length suits average heights only
40V pack is heavier than the 20V ones

products.name: Black+Decker 40V MAX 13 in. String Trimmer and Edger with Telescoping Pole
products.description:
The telescoping pole is the difference here. An adjustable shaft lets a tall user set the head so they do not stoop, and lets a short user shorten it for control, which is a bigger comfort gain than any spec on the box. It also gives a PowerCommand dial that chooses between maximum power for thick weeds and maximum runtime for long edges.

The dial is useful because a single battery has to cover very different jobs. On the runtime setting you can trim a long fence line without a recharge, and on the power setting the transmission pushes harder through tall grass at a cost to the run. It is a real advantage over the fixed-speed 20V models.

The pole has a clamp that can loosen with use, so check it before each session, and clean the shaft joint of grit. The 13 inch swath and 40V battery match the main kit above. If you are over six feet or under five and a half, the adjustability is worth having. A household with two users of different heights gets the most from it, because each person can set the shaft in ten seconds and avoid wrist strain. Keep a note of the clamp setting that suits each person so the head does not slip.
products.bestFor: Users at either end of the height range and long edging jobs.
pros: Adjustable telescoping pole fits all heights
PowerCommand dial trades power for runtime
POWERDRIVE transmission adds string torque
13 inch swath with edger conversion

products.name: Black+Decker 40V MAX 13 in. String Trimmer and Edger, Far Reach, Tool Only
products.description:
This is the bare-tool version for people who already own 40V MAX batteries. It adds a longer, far-reach shaft, so you can trim under hedges and fences without a deep stoop, and the same power adjustment dial as the telescoping model chooses between strength and runtime.

The enhanced transmission boosts motor output at the cutting string, which is how the brand gets a modest motor to cut thick growth. It is a good fit for a household that already has the batteries from a mower or sweeper, because the saving of a bare tool is then real.

The tradeoff is clear: no battery and no charger in the box, so a first-time buyer pays more than for the kit. Keep the guard clean, replace the line before it shortens below the guard edge and store the battery indoors. If you do not own 40V batteries, buy the kit instead. Because the shaft is longer than the standard model, balance shifts slightly toward the head, so try holding it with your lead hand closer to the motor. Used that way, it is comfortable for trimming under low rails and along fence bottoms.
products.bestFor: Owners of 40V MAX batteries who want a longer shaft.
pros: Extended shaft helps under hedges and fences
Power dial chooses strength or runtime
Enhanced transmission at the string
Bare tool saves money for owners

products.name: Black+Decker 20V MAX EASYFEED 12 in. String Trimmer and Edger, 2-Speed
products.description:
EASYFEED is the feature that sets this model apart. A push button advances the line, so there is no bumping the head on the ground and no tool-fighting when the string runs short, and it removes the most common annoyance of a string trimmer. The 12 inch swath is a little narrower than the 40V models and the two speeds let you boost power or stretch runtime.

PowerDrive transmission increases torque at the string, so this small 20V machine cuts better than its battery size suggests. It is light and easy to handle, and for a small to medium lawn it is the most comfortable tool in the lineup.

As always with small batteries, runtime is the limit: expect a short session on high speed and plan to swap or recharge on a larger lawn. Clear grass from under the guard after each use and keep the battery away from cold sheds. The 12 inch swath is a little narrower than the 40V tools, but on a small lawn the difference in time is a minute or two. Many owners value the lighter feel more than the extra width, especially for edging beds one-handed.
products.bestFor: Small and medium lawns where convenience matters.
pros: Push-button line advance, no bumping
Two speeds for power or runtime
PowerDrive transmission adds torque
Light and easy to handle
cons: Small battery on a larger lawn

products.name: Black+Decker 20V MAX String Trimmer, Edger and Sweeper Combo, Two Batteries
products.description:
This kit is two tools on one platform: a string trimmer that converts to a wheeled edger, and a sweeper to clear clippings from paths. It ships with two batteries and a charger, so one can charge while you use the other, and an automatic line feed system supplies line as needed.

The combination is where it earns its place. After edging a driveway, a sweeper clears the debris in minutes without hauling out a blower, and the shared battery makes it cheaper than buying the tools separately. The trimmer itself is a lightweight, quiet design for small yards.

The tradeoff is power: a 20V system is for ordinary weeds and lawn edges, not brush. Wipe the head after each session, keep the batteries indoors and replace the line before it gets short. If you have a small yard with hard surfaces, this is the practical choice. With two batteries you can rotate them so one is always ready, and the shared platform means a future purchase such as a hedge trimmer needs no new charger. Keep the sweeper nozzle clear of grass clippings so it does not lose air speed.
products.bestFor: Small yards with paths and drives to keep clear.
pros: Two batteries and a sweeper in one kit
Automatic line feed supplies string as needed
Converts to a wheeled edger
Light and quiet for small yards
cons: Sweeper adds a second tool to store

products.name: Black+Decker 40V MAX LCC340C String Trimmer and Sweeper Combo, Battery and Charger
products.description:
The LCC340C pairs the LST140 trimmer with the LSW40 sweeper, both on 40V MAX. The trimmer has a power drive transmission and automatic feed spool, and the sweeper moves air at up to 130 mph, which is enough to clear light debris from hard surfaces.

Compared with the 20V combo it has more battery energy and a stronger trimmer, but only one battery in the kit. That means one session at a time, and a recharge before you start the sweeper if the trimmer drained the pack. The price tier is the highest in the lineup because it includes two tools.

It makes sense if you already own 40V tools or plan to build a set around the platform. Clean the spool housing, store the battery indoors and check the sweeper intake for clogs. Otherwise the 13 inch 40V kit above is the simpler choice. If you buy this one, consider a spare battery from the start, because a single pack serving two tools is its real weak point. A spare also lets you edge and sweep in one visit without waiting for a recharge.
products.bestFor: Households building a 40V Black+Decker tool set.

Power drive transmission and AFS feed
Sweeper air speed up to 130 mph
Battery and charger included
cons: Only one battery for two tools

buyingCriteria.explanation: Black+Decker sells string trimmers on both. The 20V MAX models are lighter and cheaper, and the 40V MAX models run a 13 inch swath with more battery. The packs do not fit across the two platforms, so decide which you want before buying a bare tool.

EASYFEED on the 12 inch 20V model advances line with a button, and the combos use an automatic feed spool. Automatic and push-button systems save the bumping of a basic head, but can use more line. For a small yard the convenience is worth it.

The telescoping and far-reach 40V models have a dial that chooses between maximum power and maximum runtime. The EASYFEED 20V has two speeds. A control like this lets one battery cover both thick weeds and long edges.

The telescoping 40V model adjusts for height, the far-reach 40V model has a long fixed shaft and the rest are fixed length. Matching the shaft to your height saves your back more than extra power does.
The 13 inch 40V kit, the 20V combo and the 40V combo include batteries. The far-reach tool does not. The 20V combo has two batteries, the 40V combo only one.
A combo with a sweeper makes sense if you have hard surfaces to clear after edging. If you only have a lawn, the single trimmer is lighter and cheaper to store.

cards.label: 20V MAX
cards.text: The EASYFEED and combo kits are lighter and cheaper. They suit small lawns and ordinary weeds.

cards.label: 40V MAX
cards.text: The 13 inch kits and combo have more battery and a wider swath. They suit larger lawns and tougher growth.

howToChoose.note: Choose 20V for a small lawn and 40V for anything over a quarter acre.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for quick trimmer-to-edger conversion and a wheel guide. Edging puts the line vertical and wears it fast, so automatic feed helps.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The 40V 13 inch kit converts in seconds, and the 20V combo adds a wheeled edger and a sweeper. Either handles driveway edges well.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Spend more if your lawn is large or your edges are long. The 40V telescoping model's power dial stretches runtime.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Save if your lawn is small. The 20V EASYFEED does the job and is lighter.

maintenance.why: Wet clippings pack under the guard and strain the motor. Brush them out with the battery removed. Packed grass also holds moisture against the housing, which over a season can corrode the motor contacts and shorten the tool's life.
Short line cuts a narrow swath and loads the motor unevenly. Fit fresh line before it reaches the guard edge.
On the adjustable model a loose clamp lets the head droop. Tighten it.
Cold lowers capacity. Keep them at half charge.
Leaves clog the intake and cut airflow. Clear it with the battery removed.

faq.q: Which Black+Decker trimmer is best for a small lawn?
faq.a: The 20V MAX EASYFEED 12 inch is light and has a push-button feed, which removes bumping. For a lawn over a quarter acre, the 40V 13 inch kit is better.

faq.q: What does the PowerCommand dial do?
faq.a: It switches between maximum power for thick weeds and maximum runtime for long edges. It lets one battery serve both jobs. Start on the runtime setting for a long edge and flip to power only where the string slows in thick growth, so you do not drain the pack early.

faq.q: Do I need a combo with a sweeper?
faq.a: Only if you have paths and drives to clear after edging. For a lawn only, a single trimmer is lighter and cheaper.

They handle ordinary weeds and grass. Thick brush and woody stems need a brushless or gas trimmer. Forcing a line trimmer through woody growth wraps the head and can burn out the motor, so cut those stems first with loppers.

faq.q: How long does a battery last?
faq.a: It depends on speed and growth. The 20V models run shorter than the 40V ones, and the high-power setting drains faster.
Only within the same platform. 20V MAX and 40V MAX packs do not fit each other's tools.
